proposals.name: Microlensed red source
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point lens is increasingly magnifying a steady, very red background source close to the Galactic plane, superposed on its constant baseline light. The resulting achromatic amplification grows in both bands while preserving the observed g-r colour of about 1.2 mag, overwhelming the failed supernova and null forecasts.
proposals.predicts: The transient should brighten achromatically to one symmetric peak and then decline symmetrically back to its original constant baseline and colour, without supernova-like colour evolution.

proposals.name: Galactic microlensing event
proposals.idea: At b=-5 degrees a foreground point lens is increasingly magnifying a reddened background star, giving the steady then accelerating achromatic rise from day -30 with constant g-r about 1.2. The Type Ia fit mistook the long approach for a supernova rise and predicted a peak and fade, while the magnification is still growing toward closest approach.
proposals.predicts: Flux will keep rising achromatically with unchanged g-r to a symmetric peak at t0 and then decline as the time-reverse of the rise, rather than decaying and reddening like a supernova.

proposals.name: Crowded-field subtraction drift
proposals.idea: A bright red neighbour in this low-latitude crowded field is imperfectly subtracted, and seeing or zero-point drift lets increasing PSF-wing light leak into the aperture. This creates a spurious, very red, steadily brightening residual with no true transient at the nominal position.
proposals.predicts: Flux will keep growing approximately linearly, faster in r than g, with an offset non-PSF dipole in the stamps, rather than peaking and fading as a centred point source like the Ia model.

proposals.name: Foreground point microlens
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point lens at low Galactic latitude is magnifying a steady, red background source, producing the slow-then-rapid brightening misread as a Type Ia supernova. The nearly constant g-r colour as both bands rise by the same factor is the lens signature, with the constant component accounting for the unlensed baseline flux.
proposals.predicts: It predicts a further achromatic rise to a single symmetric peak followed by a mirror-image decline to the pre-event baseline at unchanged colour, not the colour-evolving asymmetric fade of a supernova.

proposals.name: Galactic microlensing event
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground lens in the crowded Galactic plane (b=-5 deg) is aligning with a distant red background star, magnifying it rather than any explosion occurring. The months-long slow rise that accelerates sharply after day -13 with persistently red g-r about 1.2 is the achromatic approach to maximum magnification on top of the steady baseline source.
proposals.predicts: The light curve will keep rising achromatically at constant colour to a symmetric peak and then fall as the mirror image of its rise, unlike a Type Ia supernova which would turn over asymmetrically and evolve in colour.
